rationale: The SR1 mutant genuinely reintroduces an overlap violation: it changes the lo-side window guard from requiring cnt >= duty+2 to cnt >= duty, which collapses the mandated two-cycle dead-time gap at the duty boundary to zero cycles and produces at least one cycle where pwm_hi and pwm_lo are both registered high for duty>=3. This is exactly the SR1 vulnerability the harness is supposed to catch (mutual exclusion of pwm_hi/pwm_lo). Yet the validation report and analyzer both confirm the SR1 check (mutants_targeting=1, mutants_detected=0) did not catch it -- the differential trace shows the mutant/vulnerable run passing SR1 despite failing FR1-FR4/SR2. This points to the check's overlap assertion being starved or short-circuited: likely the fail-fast/bookkeeping logic in scenario_fr2_sr1 stops accumulating or reporting SR1 failures once an FR2 mismatch is recorded in the same iteration, or the overlap probe is only evaluated under conditions that don't intersect with where this specific mutant's overlap actually occurs (e.g. only checked during the FR2 sweep pass, not independently across the full duty x en-toggle matrix). Since mutation_score (0.833) and discrimination_coverage (0.833) both fall below the full-coverage bar due to this single uncovered SR1 gap, and the evaluator issue is a genuine detection gap rather than a defective mutant, this must be fixed in the evaluation framework, not the mutant or spec.
revision_instructions: The SR1 no-overlap check must be strengthened so it independently and unconditionally detects any cycle where pwm_hi and pwm_lo are simultaneously high, decoupled from FR2's fail-fast bookkeeping. Concretely: in the test harness (evaluation/tb_top.v and evaluate.py), the overlap assertion (pwm_hi & pwm_lo)==0 must be evaluated and its own failure counter incremented on every single clock edge across the full duty=0..15 sweep with randomized/held en toggling over at least 3 periods -- and this SR1 failure counter must NOT be gated, skipped, or suppressed by an FR2 mismatch occurring in the same iteration or scenario. Ensure SR1 is checked as a standalone pass over the full waveform independent of whether FR1-FR4 already failed on that cycle, so that a submission which reintroduces even a single cycle of pwm_hi/pwm_lo overlap (for example, by narrowing or removing the two-cycle dead-time gap at the duty boundary so the low-side window opens too early) is guaranteed to be caught and reported as an SR1 FAIL regardless of other requirement outcomes. Verify this fix by confirming a submission whose only defect is a collapsed dead-time gap at the duty transition boundary (causing a genuine one-or-more-cycle overlap between the two outputs) is flagged as SR1 FAIL by the harness.rn`, even when other requirement checks also fail on the same run.'.replace('n`,','.')
